hints.title: K-Transaction Upper Bound Obstacle
hints.text: You may complete at most k non-overlapping transactions. How can generalizing the finite state machine across k sequential buy and sell stages compute the maximum possible profit?

hints.title: K-Tier State Array Invariant
hints.text: For transaction t from 1 to k, buy[t] = max(buy[t], sell[t - 1] - price) and sell[t] = max(sell[t], buy[t] + price).

hints.title: Dual 1D State Array Iteration Procedure
hints.text: If k >= len(prices) // 2, greedily accumulate all positive daily differences. Otherwise, initialize buy array of size k + 1 to -infinity and sell array of size k + 1 to 0. For each price p, loop t from 1 to k: update buy[t] to max(buy[t], sell[t - 1] - p) and sell[t] to max(sell[t], buy[t] + p). Return sell[k].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of days in prices
complexity.notes: Iterates through N prices, updating K buy and sell transaction states.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all transaction boundary configurations takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two 1D arrays of size K + 1 use O(K) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Short-circuiting to greedy accumulation when k >= n // 2 to avoid wasted computation.
